title: Analog square lead
notes:
The machine top line. The shelf's nine leads are six guitars and three acoustic soloists, so the club kits (`drums/club-kit`, `drums/machine-808`) and the machine low end (`bass/moog-sub`) had nothing above them that belonged to the same record — every available melody voice was a player in a room. This is the missing half: `moog-sub`'s argument, an octave and a half up and pointed at the tune.

**No `body`, no `breath`, no `vibrato`, and that is the design.** Those three blocks exist to say *a physical object made this*, and nothing did. Forked from `lone-whistle` — the purest thing on the shelf — precisely so all three could be deleted rather than tuned down: the whistle is a mouth and this is a voltage, and half-modelling a mouth is what makes a synth lead sound like a bad flute. Perfectly stationary pitch is normally the loudest synth tell there is; here it is the point, and the only irregularity in the sound is the 12 cents between the two oscillators.

**`fatsquare`, not saw.** The hollow odd-harmonic spectrum is the same choice `moog-sub` makes and for the same reason — it leaves the even harmonics free, which is where a saw lead and a distorted guitar collide. Two oscillators at 12 cents, because two perfectly-tuned oscillators sum to one oscillator. Not more: this is one synthesiser, not a section, and a wide supersaw spread would put it in the pad's territory.

**A resonant filter envelope is the articulation.** `-24 dB` rolloff with Q at 3 — steeper and more resonant than any guitar voice here, which all sit under 1.5. Base 300 Hz opening 3.6 octaves, decaying to a 0.4 sustain in 250 ms: every note has a downward sweep in it, which is the sound of a sequenced line rather than a played one. Turn the sustain up and it flattens into an organ; take the Q past about 5 and each note whistles its own cutoff pitch over the tune.

**No amp.** Not an omission — the amp's fixed power stage grits everything it touches, and grit here reads as a broken speaker rather than as drive. If this ever wants dirt it should get it from the composition's own chain, not from a guitar rig.

Polyphony 3: two for the twin-lead thirds this repo writes by default, one spare so a phrase can overlap itself at the seam.
summary: Square synth lead with no body, breath or vibrato at all. The machine top line for the club kits; every other lead is a player in a room.
